question: The New Year as per the Assamese calendar coincides with the beginning of the harvest season, which is also known as ______ Bihu.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Bohag Bihu**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Bohag Bihu**, also known as **Rongali Bihu**, marks the Assamese New Year and the beginning of the harvest season.
 
• It is celebrated in the month of **April**, typically on the 14th or 15th, and aligns with the harvest festivals in other parts of India like Tamil Nadu's **Puthandu** and Punjab's **Baisakhi**.
 
• This festival spans **three primary days**: Goru Bihu (for cattle), Manuh Bihu (for humans), and Gosai Bihu (for deities).
 
• Bohag Bihu involves traditional dances like the **Bihu dance**, music, and the preparation of delicacies such as **pithas** (rice cakes) and **larus** (sweet snacks).
 
• The festival is rooted in agrarian traditions, celebrating fertility, prosperity, and the bond between humans and nature.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Other Types of Bihu:**

 
 
• **Magh Bihu:** Also known as Bhogali Bihu, it is the post-harvest festival celebrated in January, emphasizing feasts and bonfires.
 
• **Kati Bihu:** Observed in October, it is a simpler festival focused on lighting lamps in paddy fields to pray for a good harvest.
 
 
 
• **Agrarian Connection:** Bihu festivals are directly linked to the agricultural cycle of Assam, reflecting the socio-economic dependence on farming.
 
• **Cultural Significance:** Bohag Bihu is a symbol of Assamese identity and unity, transcending religious and ethnic boundaries in the state.
 
• **Bihu Dance:** Recognized worldwide, it is a vibrant folk dance that showcases the energy and spirit of the Assamese people, performed during the festival.
 
• **Assamese Calendar:** Bohag Bihu marks the start of the Assamese calendar year, aligning with the traditional Hindu solar calendar.
